guitar.evidence: Dan Auerbach is well documented as a collector and user of vintage budget guitars (Harmony, Supro, Guild, Silvertone) and Gibsons, giving The Black Keys their fuzzy, lo-fi blues-rock tone.

tone.target: gritty fuzz-leaning garage rock crunch with bright bite
tone.profile: gritty fuzz-leaning garage rock crunch with bright bite
tone.summary: A high-gain signal chain utilizing Fuzz distortion into a classic UK combo amp model, paired with a punchy 2x12 cabinet to achieve garage rock bite and thick riff attack.

rig.name: The Black Keys - Gold On The Ceiling - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise inherent in high-gain fuzz circuits.
Provide the core fuzzy edge and raw garage drive required for The Black Keys sound.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative fuzz, but 'Fuzz' model is more classic/raw.

blocks.purpose: Add a secondary layer of grit and bite (like a dirty boost) without sounding like smooth blues overdrive.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here to simulate the punchy, slightly overdriven character often found in garage rock pedals.

alternatives.reason: Might be too clean or focused on blues tones.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a small-to-mid British combo amp, providing the necessary raw power and bite.

alternatives.reason: Also suitable, but UK 50 often captures a slightly punchier, more aggressive tone.

blocks.purpose: Match the clue for a smaller cabinet (1x12 or 2x12) and provide punchy low-mids.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is chosen over UK/Mess cabs to better match the 'punchy', American garage rock feel while keeping it small.

alternatives.reason: Too large and might muddy the tight low end.

blocks.purpose: Fine-tune the tone to emphasize bright bite and tight low end while reducing excessive mid-scoop.
Included as a potential subtle texture layer if needed, but kept inactive to avoid lush modulation.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is generally avoided for this genre, but it's included in the chain structure. It will be left off/inactive by default.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and raw lo-fi grit without sounding overly processed or lush.
blocks.gap: A very low mix is used to simulate the natural room sound of a garage recording, rather than a dedicated reverb effect.

alternatives.reason: Too clean and artificial for this raw tone.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the raw, punchy sound of vintage garage rock.

proposals.reason: The current US 2x12 might be too clean; a vintage IR will add necessary lo-fi grit and raw character.
